answer: Each Sybil identity must post its own bond plus a deposit of work that honest peers already graded, so a thousand puppet accounts need a thousand separate capitals rather than one. Random grading seats add a ripple of unpredictable cross-checks, so a sybil ring cannot grade its own flaky output, each fake account just another chip of shale. Withdrawal waits through a long unbonding window, letting peers raise a signal during a surge of new accounts. Cost scales linearly while payout stays flat, so farming turns loss-making well before the ring captures one percent of supply.
